# Results

## Stiffness-dependent expression

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit
(@fig-stiffness). Sed ut perspiciatis unde omnis iste natus error sit
voluptatem accusantium doloremque laudantium, totam rem aperiam
(@tbl-summary). Expression increased with substrate stiffness according
to a saturating dose-response,

$$
y(E) = y_{\min} + \frac{y_{\max} - y_{\min}}{1 + \left(\mathrm{EC}_{50}/E\right)^{h}},
$$ {#eq-hill}

where $h$ is the Hill coefficient and $\mathrm{EC}_{50}$ the stiffness of
half-maximal response. Fitting @eq-hill to the data in @fig-stiffness gave
$\mathrm{EC}_{50} = 8.3 \pm 1.1\ \mathrm{kPa}$ (mean $\pm$ SE; @eq-se).

```{r}
#| label: fig-stiffness
#| fig-cap: "**Substrate stiffness increases target-gene expression.** Normalized expression of *tnfa* in gut organoids cultured on hydrogels of increasing Young's modulus, by microbiota treatment (n = 12 per group; simulated data). Points are individual organoids; lines are Hill fits (@eq-hill)."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.5
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(610)
d <- expand.grid(E = c(1, 3, 10, 30, 100), mb = c("Conventional", "Germ-free"),
                 rep = 1:12)
hill <- function(E, ymax) 1 + (ymax - 1) / (1 + (8.3 / E)^1.6)
d$expr <- hill(d$E, ifelse(d$mb == "Conventional", 6, 3)) +
  rnorm(nrow(d), sd = 0.4)
ggplot(d, aes(E, expr, color = mb)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.05, alpha = 0.5, size = 1.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Young's modulus E (kPa)", y = "Relative expression",
       color = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Statistical analysis

For each group we report the mean and its standard error,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bar{y} &= \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} y_i, &
\mathrm{SE} &= \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-se}

with $s$ the sample standard deviation. Dose-response parameters were
estimated by nonlinear least squares fits of @eq-hill. All analyses used R;
the complete code is embedded in this document's source (`.qmd`), so
rendering it reproduces every number, figure, and table above.
